pairs: Jacob quoque abiit itinere quo cœperat:
Likewise, Jacob continued on the journey that he had begun.
And the Angels of God met him.
et appellavit nomen loci illius Mahanaim,
And he called the name of that place Mahanaim,
Then he also sent messengers before him to his brother Esau,
et nuntios ante se ad Esau fratrem suum in terram Seir,
“You shall speak in this way to my lord Esau:
et fui usque in præsentem diem.
and I have been with him until the present day.
mittoque nunc legationem ad dominum meum,
And now I send an ambassador to my lord,
ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo.
so that I may find favor in your sight.”’”
And the messengers returned to Jacob,
et ecce properat tibi in occursum cum quadringentis viris.
and behold, he rushes to meet you with four hundred men.”
et perterritus divisit populum qui secum erat,
And in his terror, he divided the people who were with him,
likewise the flocks, and the sheep,
Si venerit Esau ad unam turmam,
and God of my father Isaac,
O Lord who said to me:
and to the place of your nativity,
and I will do well for you.’
I am less than any of your compassions and your truth,
et veritate tua quam explevisti servo tuo.
which you have fulfilled to your servant.
In baculo meo transivi Jordanem istum:
With my staff I crossed over this Jordan.
et nunc cum duabus turmis regredior.
And now I go back with two companies.
Erue me de manu fratris mei Esau,
Rescue me from the hand of my brother Esau,
for I am very afraid of him,
ne forte veniens percutiat matrem cum filiis.
lest perhaps he may come and strike down the mother with the sons.
Tu locutus es quod benefaceres mihi,
You did say that you would do well by me,
et dilatares semen meum sicut arenam maris,
and that you would expand my offspring like the sand of the sea,
quæ præ multitudine numerari non potest.
which, because of its multitude, cannot be numbered.”
And when he had slept there that night,
he separated, from the things that he had,
camelos fœtas cum pullis suis triginta,
thirty milking camels with their young,
Et misit per manus servorum suorum singulos seorsum greges,
And he sent them by the hands of his servants,
and he said to his servants:
and let there be a space between flock and flock.”
Si obvium habueris fratrem meum Esau,
“If you happen to meet my brother Esau,
He has sent them as a gift to my lord Esau.
And he is also coming after us.”
Similarly, he gave orders to the second,
and to all who followed the flocks,
Iisdem verbis loquimini ad Esau cum inveneritis eum.
“Speak these same words to Esau, when you find him.
Et addetis: Ipse quoque servus tuus Jacob iter nostrum insequitur.
And you will add: ‘Your servant Jacob himself also follows after us,
“I will appease him with the gifts that go ahead,
and after this, I will see him;
perhaps he will be gracious to me.”’”
And so the gifts went before him,
ipse vero mansit nocte illa in castris.
but he himself lodged that night in the camp.
And when he had arisen early,
et totidem famulas cum undecim filiis,
and the same number of handmaids, with his eleven sons,
and he crossed over the ford of Jabbok.
Traductisque omnibus quæ ad se pertinebant,
And having delivered over all the things that belonged to him,
et ecce vir luctabatur cum eo usque mane.
And behold, a man wrestled with him until morning.
Qui cum videret quod eum superare non posset,
And when he saw that he would not be able to overcome him,
he touched the nerve of his thigh,
“Your name will not be called Jacob,
quoniam si contra Deum fortis fuisti,
for if you have been strong against God,
how much more will you prevail against men?”
by what name are you called?”
Et benedixit ei in eodem loco.
And he blessed him in the same place.
Vocavitque Jacob nomen loci illius Phanuel,
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel,
“I have seen God face to face,
et salva facta est anima mea.
and my soul has been saved.”
And immediately the sun rose upon him,
after he had crossed beyond Peniel.
Yet in truth, he limped on his foot.
Quam ob causam non comedunt nervum filii Israël,
eo quod tetigerit nervum femoris ejus,
do not eat the nerve that withered in Jacob’s thigh,
because he touched the nerve of his thigh and it was obstructed.
